RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1: "When the IPv6 VPN traffic is to be transported to the BGP speaker using IPv6 tunneling (e.g., IPv6 MPLS LSPs, IPsec-protected IPv6 tunnels), the BGP speaker SHALL advertise a Next Hop Network Address field containing a VPN-IPv6 address - whose 8-octet RD is set to zero, and - whose 16-octet IPv6 address is set to the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker." Read all three tagged carriers and producing paths. TestRFC4659ConfiguredIPv6TransportNextHopWire remains the principal sender-identity proof: native configuration creates a real Peer and recipient Session over TCP6, with self/explicit selection and both grouping modes. rfc4659RequireOwnedHostAddresses and rfc4659RefuseLocalAddress independently establish namespace ownership; the accepted endpoint supplies the self oracle, and a distinct speaker-owned loopback supplies the explicit oracle. rfc4659ReadConfiguredRoutes/rfc4659ConfiguredMPReach require AFI 2/SAFI 128, length 24, every zero-RD byte, the exact independently owned global, both literal labeled VPN NLRIs, no duplicate and completion only at VPNv6 EOR. buildMPReachVPN clears the RD and copies the selected address; vpnNextHopOctets selects the 24-byte global form for these distinct /128 fixtures. TestUpdateBuilder_BuildVPN_IPv6_NextHop remains an encoding control, not independent address-ownership proof. The changed TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair is contextual exception evidence: negotiateForwardTestFamilies now publishes identical explicit MP negotiation to Peer and Session, so the VPN family is admitted rather than absent from Session state. Its exact 48-byte zero-RD/unspecified-global/zero-RD/link-local assertion, endpoint distinction, unicast exclusion and invalid-case withdrawals are unchanged. Section 3.2.1.1 also says: "If the BGP speakers peer using only their link-local IPv6 address (for example, in the case where an IPv6 CE peers with an IPv6 PE, where the CE does not have any IPv6 global address, and where eBGP peering is achieved over the link-local addresses), the "unspecified address" ([V6ADDR]) is used by the advertising BGP speaker to indicate the absence of the global IPv6 address in the Next Hop Network Address field." applyEgressNextHopScope, vpnIPv6LinkLocalPeering and egressNextHopWithheld consume that exception on both forwarding rails; it does not license an unspecified IPv6-unicast global. Preserve the positive-only annotation: this is a conditional sender-emission obligation, not receiver rejection. Section 3.2.1 leaves transport-policy definition to the operator. Evidence remains control-plane configured origination, not tunnel creation, IPv4-mapped transport, whole 48-byte origination or PE/ASBR dataplane support. The old comment-only-change narrative is superseded by the real negotiated-family repair. No new semantic defect found; runtime renewal and stamping remain parent-owned, and no checks were run here.
